A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FastVLM and contain readable main text, figures, tables, and complete supplementary material. The original architecture and experiments can be matched across relocation, renumbering, and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy and latency measurements, architectural ablations, resolution experiments, and repeated-run results for FastViT/FastViTHD-based VLMs.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds training configurations, benchmark evaluations, dynamic-resolution measurements, and qualitative failure cases.

M1.justification: v2 adds a fourth training stage: full-model fine-tuning on MammothVL instruction data containing chain-of-thought reasoning, after Stage 2 (Section 4; Appendix A, Table 9). This extends the training procedure; the FastViTHD architecture and token-reduction mechanism remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 newly evaluates CVBench-2D/3D, MathVista, and AI2D, extending explicit testing of spatial perception and visual mathematical/diagram reasoning (Tables 7 and 12). Training also incorporates DocMatix and MammothVL. ChartQA, OCRBench, and InfoVQA were already evaluated in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: The new concurrent-work comparison in Table 7 adds SmolVLM2, MolmoE A1B-7B, MM1.5-1B, and FlorenceVL-3B, substantially expanding comparisons with recent compact VLMs. LLaVA-OneVision also enters the expanded text-rich comparison in Table 11. The original main and token-pruning comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The principal scaled-data rows in Table 6 change from 11.9M to 12.5M instruction samples, with an additional 10.6M-sample Stage 3. Appendix C.1 adds 2048-resolution AnyRes configurations using 2x2 tiles of size 1024 and 1280 visual tokens. Table 7 introduces comparisons using VLMEvalKit for some baselines and lmms-eval for others; earlier controlled LLaVA-1.5 settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds six illustrative failure cases comparing two LLM sizes and two resolutions, distinguishing cases requiring more knowledge, higher resolution, or both (Tables 14–16). Appendix C.1 extends the existing tiling analysis to larger-resolution configurations. The original architectural and pooling ablations are retained.

E5.justification: v1 Table 11 and v2 Table 13 contain identical results from three independent FastViT runs and identical per-metric standard deviations. The estimated Avg-5 standard deviation remains approximately 0.1. No new uncertainty-reporting procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 6 updates five scaled-data rows and adds three Stage-3 rows; the appendices add AnyRes, CVBench/MathVista, and qualitative outcomes. For example, the earlier 7B/1024 model's 78.9 DocVQA score at 11.9M instruction samples is retained in v2 Table 11, alongside new 82.7 and 88.0 scores for 12.5M and 23.1M recipes. These reflect different training conditions.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs. The architectural reasoning, token-count relationships, and TTFT/Pareto descriptions remain substantively equivalent; the additions are empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract strengthens the LLaVA-OneVision comparison from comparable performance on SeedBench and MMMU to better performance also including DocVQA. The central contributions—efficient hybrid encoding, fewer visual tokens, and an improved resolution-latency-accuracy trade-off—remain the same.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds specific failure conditions involving small text, alignment, insufficient knowledge, and reasoning over detailed images, explaining when resolution or LLM size helps. Appendix C.1 newly interprets poorer heavily tiled performance through semantic breaks. These extend the existing encoder-decoder trade-off interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents public code/model access and identifies six released Stage-2/Stage-3 checkpoints. Appendix A supplies Stage-3 hyperparameters and trainable modules, while Appendix D.2 describes DocMatix inclusion and single-image filtering of MammothVL. These substantially extend reproducibility and access information beyond v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations and discussion for concurrent VLMs, new training sources, MathVista, and VLMEvalKit, while removing the feature-pyramid-networks reference. The central positioning against ViT encoders, token-pruning methods, and convolutional backbones remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, architectural explanations, and conclusion receive localized rewriting and terminology cleanup. v2 adds a concurrent-work paragraph, Appendix C.1/C.2, Appendix E, and acknowledgments, while retaining the main section order and narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds concurrent-work and CVBench/MathVista tables plus three image-based qualitative tables. It substantially expands the text-rich results table with model-size groups and AnyRes rows, and adds a Stage-3 column to the training table. The six original figures are retained, with several relocated.

improvement.justification: New spatial/mathematical evaluations, contemporary baselines, and concrete failure examples strengthen an already extensive empirical study; documented code/checkpoint access improves reproducibility. The gains are incremental to the retained controlled evidence. Larger training datasets and mixed evaluation frameworks limit interpretation of newer performance comparisons, and Table 11 R10 leaves one AnyRes training-data budget ambiguous.
